title: How Latino Voters Are Experiencing the 2026 Midterm Elections
summary: Democratic congressional candidates have a sizable advantage among Latino registered voters. And Latino Democratic candidate supporters are more engaged with this year’s election compared with four years ago.

title: The Economy Is the Top Issue for Latino Voters in the 2026 Midterms
summary: A majority says the Trump administration is doing too much on deportations For Latino voters, the economy is the top issue on their minds when it comes to the upcoming congressional elections, much like other registered voters. More than eight-in-ten Latino registered voters (86%) say the economy is very important to their vote for Congress […]

title: Latino Registered Voters See the Democratic Party More Favorably Than the Republican Party
summary: Latino registered voters have more positive views of the Democratic Party than the Republican Party overall. About half (53%) have a favorable opinion of the Democratic Party, higher than the 44% who said this in the months before the 2024 election. title: The Gender Gap in AI
summary: Men and women now use AI chatbots at similar rates, but men use them more often, while women are more skeptical of AI's impact on their lives.

title: Republicans’ Views of Some Countries and International Organizations Differ Widely by Age
summary: Younger Republicans’ views of some countries and international organizations are sometimes closer to Democrats’ views than they are to those of older Republicans.

title: How Do Americans Feel About G20 Countries?
summary: Ahead of this year's G20 summit, most Americans rate Australia, Canada, Japan, Italy and other members warmly. Sentiment is coldest toward Russia.

title: Online Community and Connection in America
summary: Nearly four-in-ten U.S. adults are in an online community. These virtual third spaces can take many forms, like Facebook groups, online video games or fandom forums on Reddit.

title: Many Americans Are Struggling to Afford Basic Necessities
summary: 44% of Americans had trouble paying for a basic necessity in the past year, with lower-income adults hit hardest.

summary: Since 2019, a growing share among those who say there’s too much inequality think the economic system needs to be completely rebuilt to address it.

title: Religious Groups Differ Widely in Their 2026 Midterm Preferences
summary: White evangelical Protestants and White Catholics favor Republicans in the midterms, while other religious groups split or lean Democratic.
